name: Hexyl hexanoate

pubchem.title: Hexyl Hexanoate
pubchem.description: Hexyl hexanoate is a hexanoate ester obtained by the formal condensation of the carboxy group of hexanoic acid (caproic acid) with hexan-1-ol. It is a constituent found in passion fruit, apples, strawberries and wine. It has a role as a volatile oil component, a flavouring agent, a fragrance and a plant metabolite. It is functionally related to a hexan-1-ol.

consumer_summary.what_it_is: Hexyl hexanoate is a volatile ester that helps give fruits like apples, strawberries, and passion fruit their characteristic sweet, fruity aromas. Formed naturally when hexanoic acid combines with hexanol, it is widely used as a flavoring agent and fragrance. You likely encounter it every time you enjoy a glass of wine or bite into a fresh apricot.
consumer_summary.found_in: This fragrant molecule is naturally found in everyday fruits like apples, apricots, and plantains, as well as in bitter orange and cannabis. It is also a key aromatic component that develops during wine fermentation.
consumer_summary.why_researchers_care: Researchers are primarily drawn to hexyl hexanoate for its role as a powerful odorant and signaling molecule, both in human flavor perception and insect communication. Much of the current literature focuses on how it interacts with odorant receptors, with the strongest evidence coming from human observational studies (Oxford level 2b) examining its presence in wine aerosols and fruit volatiles. Scientists are also exploring its potential ecological roles, including how it functions as a pheromone or semiochemical in various insect species.

structure_function.statement: Early animal work points toward hexyl hexanoate having potential calming properties that may support relaxation.
structure_function.basis: This rests on a single animal study exploring its effects on anxiety-like behavior.

structure_function.statement: Hexyl hexanoate is being studied for its potential to act as a natural insect repellent or behavioral modifier.
structure_function.basis: This is based on one animal study observing its effects on insect behavior and scent gland chemistry.

hypothesized_benefits.hypothesis: Researchers are exploring whether the aroma of hexyl hexanoate can directly influence the nervous system to promote calm. If this bears out, it could help explain the relaxing effects of certain fruit and wine aromatics.
hypothesized_benefits.study_to_test_it: A randomized, placebo-controlled human trial exposing healthy volunteers to hexyl hexanoate vapor via inhalation and measuring physiological stress markers like heart rate variability and salivary cortisol over a 30-minute session.

hypothesized_benefits.hypothesis: Early animal work points toward this ester acting as a semiochemical that deters certain pests, raising the question of whether it could be harnessed as a natural crop protectant or repellent.
hypothesized_benefits.study_to_test_it: A controlled field or greenhouse study applying hexyl hexanoate formulations to target crops and measuring the landing and oviposition rates of specific agricultural pests compared to a control over a two-week period.

consumer_summary.evidence_at_a_glance: Best evidence so far is human observational work (Oxford 2b) regarding its role in flavor and aerosols; the limited research into its physiological effects is currently restricted to animal and lab studies.
